item.title: Ireland's Nitrates Derogation secured until 2029, says Minister
item.description: Minister Martin Heydon's announced Ireland has secured the continued availability of the Nitrates Derogation. The Nitrates Committee of the European Commission met to extend the derogation, which expires this month, until the end of 2028 with some new conditions attached. Minister for Agriculture Martin Heydon says an extension will be positive for farmers here: Local MEP Ciaran Mullooly says the uncertainty is unfair on farmers: Advertisement

item.title: 585 Patients Waiting on Hospital Trolleys Nationwide as Pressure Mounts on Emergency Departments
item.description: 585 patients are waiting on trolleys in the country's hospitals. 396 are waiting in Emergency Departments , while 189 are in wards elsewhere in the hospital. University Hospital Limerick has the highest number of people waiting at 66. Advertisement That's followed by Cork University Hospital at 59. Sligo University Hospital is again the third highest in the country with 30 admitted patients on trolleys. item.title: Strokestown to face Glenullin
item.description: Strokestown have discovered their oppontents in the All-Ireland intermediate football semi-finals. The Roscommon side will face Ulster champions Glenullin who scored a three-15 to 19-point win over Cuchullains on Sunday in Clones. That game will be played on the third or fourth of January. Meanwhile, St. Brigid's will discover their All-Ieland semi-final oppontents when Scotstown meet Kilcoo in the Ulster final this Saturday. That fixture throws in at 6:15 at the Box-It Athletic Grounds Armagh.

item.title: 2,500 Without Power in Shannonside Region
item.description: There are over 2500 ESB customers without power in the Shannonside region. The outage comes as a result of the strong winds of Storm Bram, with the entire Shannonside region under an orange wind weather warning until this evening. The power fault in Mohill County Leitrim was reported at around twenty to three and is estimated to be restored by 10 o'clock tonight. item.title: EU Votes to Extend Ireland's Nitrates Derogation
item.description: The EU has voted to extend Ireland's nitrates derogation by three years. The current derogation was due to expire at the end of the month. Officials have confirmed new conditions, including cutting chemical nitrogen allowances and expanding buffer zones around rivers. Advertisement Longford IFA Chairperson, John Sheridan feels the renewal will be a relief to farmers, but would prefer a longer-term solution.

item.title: Local flu-related hospital admissions double in a week
item.description: The number of people hospitalised with flu in the west and northwest almost doubled last week. There were 163 patients admitted last week - compared to 87 the week before. item.title: Councillor Plans Drive-Thru Restaurant and Retail Development in Tarmonbarry
item.description: A local councillor says he has plans to develop a drive-thru restaurant and retail units in Tarmonbarry. Cllr Tom Crosby says the development would benefit both local residents and families travelling on the N5. It comes following news that the Ballaghaderreen to Scramogue bypass project is ahead of the schedule. Advertisement Mayo-based Wills Brothers Ltd plans to complete the €460 million project in 2027.
